subject: Sealed-proxy BYOK connector: key ceremony plan & attestation review
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@stellarbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: onprem-platform@stellarbank.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sealed-proxy BYOK connector — proposal & key ceremony prep

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the on-prem connector deploy for the first tranche of branches (air‑gapped racks), we want to lock down the key custody and rotation approach. Attached is a network diagram (diagram-sealed-proxy.pdf) and an initial checklist.

High level ask: we want a BYOK flow that meets our security team needs: HSM-backed root key material, an operator-led key ceremony (desktop/tabletop first), and an automated monthly rotation with strong auditability. Specific questions we hoped Redwood could confirm:
- Can the sealed-proxy pattern support an HSM local to the customer (PKCS#11) and accept a wrapped key blob from Redwood for initial seeding?
- For rolling rotations, can the runtime accept an operator-supplied wrapped key (one-time envelope) and perform a trustless swap with a quorum check?
- What's the suggested operator privilege model (just sign/unseal vs. full KMS admin)?

We propose a tabletop ceremony the week of Sep 13 and a canary install of the connector in our staging racks on Sep 20. Are those dates workable?

I've cc'd our platform team for visibility.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Head of Platform Security — StellarBank
attachments: diagram-sealed-proxy.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@stellarbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, onprem-platform@stellarbank.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sealed-proxy BYOK connector — proposal & key ceremony prep

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear writeup and the diagram. I've read through and sketched a few clarifications below; attaching a fillable attestation template (attestation-template.docx) that our compliance team can use during the ceremony.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, sealed-proxy can accept an initial wrapped key blob generated by Redwood. We support PKCS#11 HSMs and a simple envelope format (AES‑GCM with HSM wrapping metadata).
- The runtime supports a quorum-based swap: a new key blob is only accepted if N-of-M operator signatures are present (we recommend 3-of-5 for high-sensitivity customers). The swap is atomic from the perspective of serving nodes.
- Operator privileges: we recommend a split model — operators can perform sealing/unsealing and key activation but cannot export raw key material. Only the HSM operator (customer side) holds an export capability if their HSM supports it.

A few follow-ups and potential gotchas so we can align the tabletop agenda:
1) Attestation: do you plan to do TPM/AVB attestation from the sealed-proxy host to validate firmware? If yes, we will include that check in the startup sequence.
2) Audit stream: you mentioned monthly rotation + audit — we need to confirm where you want the audit stream (Redwood-hosted telemetry, or push to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS?).
3) Bootstrap fallback: if the wrapped blob fails validation during first boot, what's your desired recovery? (Rollback to previous blob, or manual operator recovery procedure?)

Proposed timeline: tabletop week of Sep 13 (we can do 13–15), staging canary Sep 20–23, production target Oct 4 (tentative).

I'll pull in Naomi for legal/compliance notes and Kimberly for ops detail.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Architect, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
Attachments: attestation-template.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@stellarbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, onprem-platform@stellarbank.com
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sealed-proxy BYOK connector — proposal & key ceremony prep

Adding ops/controls detail from our side. My thinking is intentionally conservative given regulator posture \u2014 we can relax with explicit waivers, but flagging requirements we believe will be necessary: 

- No remote unseal by Redwood: initial key material should be supplied and sealed with customer HSM. Redwood will not retain an unencrypted copy. Our design treats Redwood as an attestation/verification and orchestration plane only.
- Split custody for bootstrap: recommend 3-of-5 operator signatures where at least one sig must originate from your on‑prem security team. This ensures the customer retains a gate.
- Rotation cadence & lifetimes: monthly rotation is fine; however we recommend a staged lifecycle where intermediate keys (used for wrapping) have 90-day validity and root HSM material only rotates on strict events (regulatory or key compromise).
- Audit and evidence: attach operation-checklist.xlsx for ceremony runbook. All operator actions must emit signed audit events and an immutable record pushed to your SIEM. Redwood can provide signed proof artifacts (timestamped hashes) but not the private key material.
- Emergency recovery: define an "operator zeroize" play that requires two distinct executives to authorize a wipe. Technical implementation: an HSM policy that requires a dual‑token approval for zeroize.

Operational question: do you want the sealed-proxy to perform local tokenization (i.e., keep short‑lived session keys) or should session tokens be proxied through Redwood-hosted cache? For air‑gapped racks we recommend fully local tokenization.

I'll be prepared to run the tabletop on Sep 14 (09:00 PT) if that works for everyone.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: operation-checklist.xlsx

Tessa / Kimberly — thank you, this is very helpful.

We agree with the conservative defaults (no remote unseal, split custody, signed audit stream). Local tokenization is our preference for air‑gapped racks. Sep 14 at 09:00 PT for the tabletop works for our leads; we'll reserve a conference room and have our on‑prem ops team run through the checklist.

A couple of clarifications before the tabletop:
- For the N-of-M signatures: we will bring three signers from our side (two platform engineers + one security officer). Please confirm Redwood will supply the operator signing UX + the signing key distribution instructions ahead of time.
- For the attestation template: we will pre-fill the initial hardware fingerprint fields and return it to you before the ceremony.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to send the operator signing guide and a short demo recording by Sep 9.
2) StellarBank to confirm signer list and provide HSM vendor/model.
3) Run tabletop 2026-09-14 09:00 PT.

I'll attach an updated diagram post‑tabletop. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Maria Santos
Head of Platform Security — StellarBank
